ing: Dominican style or any firm salami, sliced
st: Toss the sliced red onion with [[0.25 cup]] vinegar, [[0.25 cup]] water, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Let it pickle while you cook.
Cut the ends off each plantain, slit the skin lengthwise, and peel it with a knife. Cut into thick chunks.
Put the plantains in a pot, cover with water, add [[1 tsp]] salt, and boil for 20 to 25 minutes until very soft.
Scoop out about a cup of the cooking water, then drain the plantains.
Mash the hot plantains with [[3 tbsp]] butter and a splash of the reserved water, adding more water until the texture is smooth and soft like mashed potatoes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and fry the salami slices 2 minutes per side until browned. Move to a plate.
Fry the cheese slices in the same pan for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Fry the eggs in [[2 tbsp]] oil until the whites are set.
Pile the mangú on plates, top with the pickled onions, and serve with the salami, cheese, and eggs.
Toss the chicken with the lime juice, half the garlic, [[1 tsp]] oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper. Marinate 20 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil with [[1 tsp]] sugar in a wide pot over medium heat for 1 minute, then brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side.
Add half the onion and bell pepper, the tomatoes, and [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste. Stir, add [[1 cup]] water, cover, and simmer 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
For the beans, heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a saucepan and cook the remaining onion, bell pepper, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[1 tsp]] oregano, then add the beans with their liquid, the cilantro, and [[1 cup]] water.
Simmer the beans uncovered for 20 minutes, mashing a few against the pot to thicken. Add [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
For the rice, heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot, stir in the rinsed rice for 1 minute, then add [[3.5 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Boil until the water level drops to the rice, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Serve the rice, beans, and chicken together on one plate.

ing: or white sweet potato, peeled and cubed
st: Season the chicken, pork, and beef with the lime juice, half the garlic, the oregano, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Let sit 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef and pork in batches, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Pour in [[10 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer for 20 minutes more.
Add the cassava, yams, plantains, and squash and simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the corn and half the cilantro and cook 10 minutes more, until the roots are very soft and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Mash a few chunks of root against the pot to thicken the broth. Add [[1 tsp]] salt to taste.
Stir in the remaining cilantro and serve hot with white rice and sliced avocado.
Season the chicken with half the garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil and [[1 tsp]] sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat until the sugar turns amber, about 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and brown for 4 minutes per side.
Stir in the onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic and cook 4 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and remaining oregano and stir for 2 minutes until darker.
Pour in the rinsed rice and stir for 1 minute to coat in the paste.
Add the [[3.5 cups]] hot water, the olives, cilantro, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Boil until the liquid reaches the top of the rice.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes. The chicken must reach 165°F (74°C).
Rest 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, and serve.
Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, bell pepper, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the drained pigeon peas and olives and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, [[1 cup]] coconut milk, [[2.25 cups]] water, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, and the cilantro. Stir once.
Boil over high heat, uncovered, until the liquid drops to the level of the rice, about 8 minutes.
Stir once from the bottom, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff gently with a fork, and serve.

ing: skin-on if possible, cut in 1.5-inch chunks
st: Toss the pork belly with the lime juice, garlic, oregano, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Put the pork and marinade in a wide heavy pan with [[1 cup]] water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, about 30 minutes, until the water has evaporated and the fat starts to render.
Pat the pieces dry with paper towels if there is any liquid left.
Add [[0.5 cup]] oil to the pan and raise the heat to medium-high.
Fry the pork 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until deeply golden and crisp on all sides. Stand back as it spits.
Move to paper towels and sprinkle with the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Serve hot with tostones and lime wedges.
Cut off the plantain ends, slit the skin lengthwise, and peel it off with a knife. Cut into 1-inch thick rounds.
Stir the crushed garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt into [[1 cup]] warm water in a shallow bowl.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 325°F (165°C), about 1 inch deep.
Fry the rounds in batches for 3 minutes per side until pale golden and soft.
Move them to paper towels. While warm, smash each to 1/3 inch thick between two sheets of parchment with a plate or bottle.
Dip each smashed piece quickly into the garlic water and pat dry with paper towels so it does not spatter.
Raise the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry the pieces for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain, sprinkle with the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and serve hot with lime wedges.
Mix the ground beef with the chopped half of the onion, garlic, oregano, [[0.75 tsp]] salt, and the pepper. Shape into 4 thin patties.
Toss the shredded cabbage with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Stir the mayonnaise and ketchup together for the sauce.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side until browned and 160°F (71°C) inside.
Toast the buns cut-side down in the pan for 1 minute.
Spread sauce on both halves of each bun, then layer the patty, cabbage, tomato slices, and sliced onion.
Close the buns and serve right away.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease an 8x8-inch baking dish.
Slice the plantains lengthwise into long strips about 1/4 inch thick.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the strips for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but [[1 tbsp]] of the oil. Cook the beef, onion, bell pepper, and garlic for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the tomatoes, olives, raisins, oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Line the bottom of the dish with half of the plantain strips, overlapping them slightly.
Spread the beef over the plantains, then sprinkle with [[1 cup]] cheese.
Cover with the remaining plantains, pour the beaten eggs over the top, and add the remaining [[1 cup]] cheese.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until set and golden. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
Slice into squares and serve warm.
Put the beans and [[1 cup]] water in a blender and puree until completely smooth.
Pour the bean puree into a large pot through a strainer, pressing with a spoon, to remove the skins.
Add [[2 cups]] more water, the cinnamon sticks, and cloves and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the diced sweet potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes until they are tender.
Stir in the coconut milk, evaporated milk, and [[0.75 cup]] sugar.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick, until it thickens like a loose pudding.
Add the raisins, vanilla, and a pinch of salt and cook 5 more minutes. Take out the cinnamon sticks and cloves.
Serve warm or chilled in small bowls, topped with crushed sweet crackers.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour two 8-inch round cake pans.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat the butter and [[1.5 cups]] sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the 4 eggs one at a time, then [[1 tsp]] vanilla and the orange zest.
Add the flour mixture in three parts, alternating with the [[0.5 cup]] orange juice, mixing just until smooth.
Divide between the pans and bake for 28 to 32 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.
Level the cake layers if domed. Spread the pineapple jam over one layer and set the second layer on top.
For the meringue, whisk the 4 egg whites, [[1 cup]] sugar, and cream of tartar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water for 4 minutes until the sugar dissolves and it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Beat the warm mixture with a mixer on high for 7 minutes until thick, glossy, and cool. Beat in [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Frost the whole cake with the meringue, making swoops with the back of a spoon. Serve the same day.
Chill the milk in the fridge until very cold. Cold milk keeps the drink smooth.
Squeeze the oranges and strain the juice. You need [[1 cup]].
Stir [[3 tbsp]] sugar into the juice until it dissolves completely.
Stir the vanilla into the cold milk.
Fill two tall glasses with the crushed ice.
Pour half the milk into each glass, then slowly pour in the sweet juice.
Stir lightly once, which gives creamy swirls, and serve immediately before it separates.
